faq.a: Frustration is the hot, stuck feeling you get when something will not work or you cannot do what you want, even when you try hard.

faq.q: Why do I feel like giving up?
faq.a: When something keeps going wrong, your brain wants the uncomfortable feeling to stop, and giving up seems the quickest way. A break or a new way usually works better.
asks: Why do I quit when things are hard?

faq.q: Is it okay to take a break?
faq.a: Yes! A short break lets your body calm down and your brain rest. Lots of people solve a problem right after coming back from a break.
asks: Should I stop when I am frustrated?

faq.q: Who can help me when I am stuck?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, an older brother or sister, or a friend who knows how. Say, "Please can you show me?"
asks: I am stuck, who do I ask?

faq.q: Why does frustration mean I am learning?
faq.a: Frustration often comes when you work on something just beyond what you can do yet. That is exactly where your brain grows the most.

facts: Psychologist Lev Vygotsky taught that we learn best with tasks a little harder than we can manage alone, which he called the zone of proximal development.
A 2019 study at the US National Institutes of Health found that people's new skills improved during short rest breaks while practising.
